PullRequest.Title: tests: prune redundant and behavior-free checks
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Remove 39 tests across 15 files in a conservative application of [prune-tests](https://github.com/caldoai/skills/blob/main/skills/prune-tests/SKILL.md). No production code changes.

The removals fall into three groups:

### 1. Redundant: identical inputs, behavior and assertions already covered (22 tests)

These are duplicate executions of retained tests, not merely tests with similar names. Surrounding setup and fixtures were checked before treating them as redundant.

| Suite | Removed | Why the retained test covers it |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Markdown renderer | 2 | The "extra whitespace" cases contain exactly the same input and assertions as the retained incomplete-link list cases; neither adds whitespace. |
| OAuth scope matching | 1 | The complex Microsoft scopes case duplicates the different-order case, including both scope arrays. |
| File-system removal | 1 | The "ends with dot" case passes the same unmodified directory as the retained simple move-removal case. It does not exercise a dotted path. |
| Editable text model | 1 | "delete empty text" supplies the same zero-length edit and expected document as "insert empty text". |
| Settings merge | 1 | The multiple-local-changes case duplicates the existing local-additions/base-unchanged case, including the updated existing setting. |
| Session type availability | 1 | The paid-plan targeting-model case uses the same configuration, entitlement and model target as the retained no-Auto case. |
| Hook command selection | 7 | The edge-case block is repeated verbatim, including hook spelling and arguments. Keep one block; retain the distinct format/compatibility cases. |
| Notebook diff service | 3 | The "fast check", reverse-kind replacement and insert/delete cases repeat retained inputs and assertions. Their names do not describe additional executed scenarios. |
| Background-command rewriting | 1 | The simple external-command case exactly repeats the retained Linux `nohup` case. |
| Test execution simplification | 1 | Two common-root cases select the same nodes from the same tree and expect the same result. |
| Extension host shutdown | 1 | The generic awaited-shutdown case duplicates the retained regression test, including the expected disposal order. |
| Extension manifest properties | 1 | Two tests pass the same browser-only manifest and expect `['web']`. |
| Text-file service | 1 | "saveAll - file" actually calls `save`, exactly like the retained "save - file" test; it provides no `saveAll` coverage. |

### 2. Cannot catch regressions in the production behavior they claim to test (15 tests)

All are in `notificationsPosition.test.ts`:

- **4 configuration tests** only write/read `TestConfigurationService`, or apply a fallback inside the test. They do not exercise production notification configuration handling.
- **3 alignment tests** exercise a test-local `getDesiredAlignment` implementation, not the notification status item.
- **4 offset tests** exercise a test-local `computeTopOffset` implementation, not toast layout. Its copied base offset is already different from production, while the tests still pass.
- **3 hide-icon tests** exercise a test-local `getHideIcon` implementation, not the notification center.
- **1 codicon test** checks generic chevron identifier strings without exercising notification behavior.

These are not literally impossible to fail: editing their local implementations or the mock can break them. The problem is that changing the corresponding production notification logic cannot make them fail. Keep the tests that call the real notification expand/collapse icon helpers.

### 3. Pin implementation details or restate TypeScript guarantees (2 tests)

In `modalEditorGroup.test.ts`, remove the tests that pin `MODAL_GROUP` to `-4`, check its JavaScript type and assert that its type alias exists. They do not exercise editor routing or modal behavior. Keep the actual modal creation, routing, lifecycle and interaction tests.

This is deliberately not a claim that all remaining repository tests have been audited. Tests with different setup, inputs or compatibility contracts were not removed merely because their bodies looked similar.

Local checks:

- `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 pnpm run build-fast --client-only` — passed.
- `git diff --name-only -- '*.ts' | xargs pnpm run oxlint` — passed for all 15 changed files.
- `git diff --name-only -z -- '*.test.ts' | xargs -0 fnm exec --using=24.22.1 ./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot` — 769 passing, 3 pending.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

(Written by Copilot)

Scenarios.Scenario: Use the editor, chat, notifications, terminal tools, settings sync, and extension services in the shipped application.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: No production code changes exist in the complete 15-file inventory. All executable changes remove test callbacks or test-local helpers; import changes are confined to test modules. Application startup, interaction, save, and shutdown paths are unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: User documents, notebook cells, extensions, chat models, and notifications retain their existing production cardinalities; this diff adds no per-item work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No production scheduling, worker, limiter, queue, or concurrency changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No production cache keys, positive/negative entries, invalidation, or coalescing change on either cold or warm execution.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every diff page is a test deletion or removal of now-unused test imports, with no production implementation modification.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static review does not measure application performance; no changed production mechanism requires a duration estimate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the parsing, model-editing, settings merge, availability, manifest classification, notification, modal-constant, and test-selection unit cases.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The runner awaits each remaining callback and its existing hooks. Removed callbacks perform fixed-fixture parsing, comparisons, model operations, or test-local calculations. No retained callback receives additional work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The PR removes 39 cases overall, including fixed-size arrays, strings, model edits, and a small stub test tree; it introduces no loops or larger fixtures.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No runner configuration or test scheduling changes; the registered callback count decreases.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. Removing standalone cases does not add cache lookups or defeat coalescing; retained tests and their setup remain in place.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: removed bodies contain the work, while setup/teardown registrations and remaining test code are preserved.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact decrease in runner time is not measured and is not treated as a proven historical regression fix.
Scenarios.Verdict: Only test execution and registration work are removed; no actionable performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the PFS move-removal tests against a temporary directory.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Per-test setup creates the temporary directory. The removed case synchronously writes two files, awaits MOVE removal, and checks existence. MOVE awaits rename and starts recursive deletion without awaiting it; teardown awaits its existing removal call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: src/vs/base/test/node/pfs/pfs.test.ts setup and removed move-removal case; src/vs/base/node/pfs.ts rimrafMove/rimrafUnlink
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Temporary mkdir, two synchronous file writes, rename, recursive rm, existence check, and teardown removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fewer fixture setup/teardown and one fewer pair of writes, MOVE removal, and existence check per complete suite execution; retained cases keep their previous counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The deleted callback executed this filesystem sequence once in addition to the retained simple MOVE case with the same two-file fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setup, synchronous writes, and rename previously delayed that test's completion; successful post-rename recursive deletion was already off its critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One removed test invocation with one directory and two files; filesystem operation counts for retained cases are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing background recursive removal may overlap subsequent work. Deleting the case removes one such background operation rather than increasing concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each case gets a random temporary directory, so no shared result cache or warm-up dependency is introduced or removed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setup/teardown and the transitive rename/background-rm implementation were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Filesystem latency and background deletion overlap depend on platform; the direction of the operation-count change is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: The diff reduces filesystem work and does not change cleanup ownership of retained cases.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The suite directly constructs one NotebookWorker. mapCells performs similarity matching, registers two model DTOs, and awaits a direct $computeDiff method call before assertions. The shared worker is disposed at suite teardown.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three fewer mapCells invocations: original/modified fixtures contain 2/2, 5/5, and 8/10 cells respectively. Six fewer registered notebook models; remaining fixture sizes are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The worker is an in-process instance here, not a newly spawned worker or IPC client. No scheduling changes are made.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: mapCells assigns fresh counter-based URIs to each pair, rather than sharing a cached diff across cases. No cache key or lifetime changes; fewer models are registered before the unchanged worker disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: suite construction, mapCells DTO conversion, direct worker calls, and disposal were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: CPU and allocation savings are not measured; no increased work is evident.
Scenarios.Verdict: Removes CPU/allocation work and model registrations without introducing any boundary or retention regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run workbench text-save, extension-host shutdown, and background-command rewrite cases.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Text-save callbacks await model resolution and save using workbenchInstantiationService's TestFileService. Extension shutdown uses mock host managers with resolved start/disconnect promises and disposal that appends to an order array. The rewriter returns command strings without executing them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Logical file-service read/save calls routed through the injected TestFileService rather than newly introduced operating-system I/O.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fewer model resolve/save sequence per suite run; remaining cases retain their existing call counts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed saveAll-named case called the same single-resource save operation as the retained save-file case, with its own per-test services.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The removed callback awaited resolve and save. No additional boundary waits move onto retained test or application critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fewer single-model save case, one fewer shutdown case containing three mock host managers, and one fewer single-command rewrite. No real process launches are added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Save resolve/save ordering and awaited host shutdown are unchanged for retained cases. Rewriting remains synchronous string processing; no subprocess concurrency exists on this test path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-test service setup and disposable cleanup remain unchanged. No new cache, retry, negative-cache, or coalescing behavior; removed cases do not own shared cache initialization required by retained cases.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: mock host start/disconnect/dispose, service injection, retained cleanup, and the rewrite implementation were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. Mock lifecycle and service setup costs decrease by the removed invocations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No new subprocess, IPC, network, database, or real filesystem fan-out is introduced; only existing test operations are removed.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass across all 15 changed files and every diff page, including focused surrounding-code tracing for filesystem removal, notebook model/diff work, mocked extension lifecycle, text-file service injection, and command rewriting. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regressions found. Test pruning alone does not establish a concrete historical performance regression fix, so no blame-based fix signal was submitted. Static read-only review; no performance measurements.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
